section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the date and occasion for the maamar, the eve of Shavuos 5749.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
The night of the 5th of Sivan,
the eve of the holiday of Shavuos,

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the famous question of why the first commandment mentions the Exodus from Egypt rather than the creation of heaven and earth, which is a greater wonder.
section.t: "I am Hashem your G-d, Who brought you out of the land of Egypt,"
This verse is the first utterance of the Ten Commandments given at the giving of the Torah on the 6th of Sivan,
after Yisrael preceded "we will do" to "we will hear"
[and ministering angels came and tied two crowns to each Jew, one corresponding to "we will do" and one corresponding to "we will hear"]
on the 5th of Sivan.
And it is brought in several discourses of our Nesi'im,
the well-known question of the great ones of Yisrael,
Behold, the creation of heaven and earth is a greater wonder than the Exodus from Egypt.
For in the Exodus from Egypt,
even though there were several miracles,
behold, in addition to this not being a sufficient explanation for why it specifically says "Who brought you out of the land of Egypt,"
since also before the Exodus from Egypt and after the Exodus from Egypt there were so many miracles,
the matter of a miracle is a change from existence to existence,
but the creation of heaven and earth is existence from nothingness.
And in addition to this that creation of existence from nothingness is a greater wonder,
behold also the G-dly power in creation of existence from nothingness is a more elevated power,
as is known
that creation of existence from nothingness is only through the power of the Awtsmoos, whose existence is from His own essence.
[And it can be said,
that the fact that the existence of the created existence is true existence,
is because its coming into being is from the Awtsmoos,
the true existence].
And why does it say "Who brought you out of the land of Egypt,"
for ostensibly it should have said "Who created heaven and earth."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that both creation and the giving of the Torah are from the Awtsmoos, renewed every moment, connecting the Exodus to the essence of the Giver.
section.t: B)
And one may add,
that this, that ostensibly it should have said "Who created heaven and earth,"
is also because the creation of heaven and earth and the giving of the Torah
("I am Hashem your G-d" is the opening of the giving of the Torah)
are related to each other.
For the creation of heaven and earth is renewed every single moment,
according to the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov on the verse,
"Forever, Hashem, Your word stands firm in the heavens"
(brought in the holy Tanya)
that the G-dly power constantly brings the created being into existence from nothingness to existence.
And since creation and coming into being of existence from nothingness is through the power of the Awtsmoos,
it is understood,
that the creation that is in every single moment is actual existence from nothingness from the Awtsmoos.
And similarly regarding the Torah,
that its giving
(and its drawing down)
is from the Awtsmoos
("Anochi" — I am),
and its drawing down from the Awtsmoos is in every moment,
as it is written,
"He gives the Torah" in the present tense,
therefore our sages said,
"Every day,
they shall be in your eyes as new,"
literally new.
